title: DNS lookups are slow inside pods

turns.user_message: Our pods make a lot of outbound HTTPS calls to external APIs. Latency went from ~50 ms to ~3 seconds. The APIs are fine — I tested from my laptop. Inside the pods it feels like DNS is slow. How do I confirm and fix?
turns.se_response_summary: 3 seconds is the canonical glibc resolver retry-timeout signature. K8s default ndots:5 + long search list = every external name like 'api.stripe.com' (2 dots) tries search domains first: api.stripe.com.<ns>.svc.cluster.local → NXDOMAIN, then .svc.cluster.local → NXDOMAIN, then .cluster.local → NXDOMAIN, finally api.stripe.com. Each is ~500ms, sums to 3s. Confirm: kubectl exec <pod> -- cat /etc/resolv.conf (expect ndots:5 + search). Then time it: time getent hosts api.stripe.com vs time getent hosts api.stripe.com. (trailing dot skips search).
hints: What does the number 3 seconds suggest about the failure mode?
Why does k8s default ndots:5 cause this for external names but not internal?

turns.user_message: Confirmed. ndots:5, search list as you described. Without trailing dot: 2.8s. With trailing dot: 47ms. So the search-expansion is the problem. What's the right fix?
turns.se_response_summary: Two equally valid fixes; pick by what you control. (A) Pod-side ndots:2 via spec.dnsConfig.options (no app change, recommended). (B) App code uses trailing dot for FQDN. DON'T use ndots:1 — breaks cluster-internal short names like 'myservice'. Validate: time getent hosts api.stripe.com from pod, expect <100ms.
hints: What's the YAML field on a pod spec to override DNS options?

turns.user_message: ndots:2 fixed it for the pods. But why is the k8s default ndots:5? Seems wasteful.
turns.se_response_summary: Two reasons: (1) K8s service DNS records have 5 dots (<svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local), so ndots:5 makes search-expansion the only way short names like 'myservice' resolve to 'myservice.<ns>.svc.cluster.local'. (2) Backward compat with apps that hardcode short names. The cost (search-amplification for external names) wasn't appreciated initially; now widely-known.
hints: Why does the k8s service-name convention 'force' ndots:5?
What's the design tradeoff — internal short names vs external lookup speed?

turns.user_message: What if it weren't ndots — what other things make pod DNS slow?
turns.se_response_summary: Common runners-up (each has a dedicated playbook): (1) k8s.fm.dns-resolution-fail — CoreDNS down/no endpoints (everything fails); (2) k8s.fm.coredns-loop-detection — forward . loops via host resolv.conf; (3) k8s.fm.networkpolicy-default-deny-too-broad — UDP/53 to coredns blocked; (4) linux.fm.conntrack-table-full — host conntrack overflow drops UDP DNS replies; (5) slow upstream DNS itself (CoreDNS metrics show).
hints: If every lookup fails (not just external), what's the likely cause?
What table on the host can fill up and silently drop UDP DNS replies?
